scenes.title: First mate
scenes.caption: Talking to firstmate, and what it would cost.
scenes.say: You asked how a talking first mate would work, and what it would cost. Here's the short version.

picture.sub: How it works, and the cost

scenes.title: Not my pick
scenes.caption: Firstmate's makers chose Amazon, not me.
scenes.say: Honestly, I didn't pick Amazon. Firstmate's makers did. Its Nova Sonic model hears your voice and speaks the answer, all in one go.

scenes.title: How it joins
scenes.caption: Your laptop talks to this PC, which talks to Amazon.
scenes.say: Your laptop records your voice and sends it through a secure tunnel to this PC. This PC talks to Amazon, so your laptop never holds a password.

scenes.title: Two tools
scenes.caption: One reads numbers. One drops work in my inbox.
scenes.say: Amazon gets two tools. One reads firstmate's records, as numbers only, never names. The other drops real work in my inbox. It can't change a project.

scenes.title: Not yet
scenes.caption: Hold a key to talk. No memory. No cutting in.
scenes.say: It can't do everything yet. You hold a key to talk, it forgets each question, and you can't cut in while it speaks.

moves.cue: You hold a key to talk

scenes.title: The cost
scenes.caption: About five pounds a month if every message were spoken.
scenes.say: If every message were spoken, it's about six dollars sixty a month, around five pounds. Most likely, a pound or two.

scenes.title: Choose
scenes.caption: Tell me A, B, or both.
scenes.say: So, which one? Amazon's voice is quick and cheap. Option A is Peter's voice, free, on this PC. Tell me A, B, or both.

faults: scene 2: Reelie is in the JSON at far-right but is not in the stage as drawn, and the mic does nothing; the person is a plain 'person' for 'You', fine, but the waves cross the mic. Keep the cast and spots the same as in later scenes.
scene 3: the laptop's lock badge covers the flow dots, and 'Amazon' sits at right in this scene.

scene 4: Amazon moved from right to left, so the cast jumps; the block sits between the inbox and the records, so it reads as if the inbox is walled off from the records rather than showing that Amazon cannot change a project. Records and inbox send nothing visible.
scene 5: a list of ticks reads as 'these are good', but these are things it cannot do yet. Ticks are the wrong sign for limits.
scene 6: money is piled by 'You' and a single coin by Amazon, with no price shown, so the amounts, around five pounds and a pound or two, are not shown.

scene 7: a music note stands for Peter's voice, and a cloud for Amazon. A note is music, not a voice or an answer. The tick and cross also make it look as though A is already chosen, but Peter asks the viewer to choose.
